- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior peak.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 0.0–0.2) and price drops, model underreacts; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights short-term momentum; apply 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is rising, model tends to overforecast; reduce forecast by 3–7% if recent sentiment is sustained above 0.8.
